summary: About one unemployed jobseeker in four reaches out to friends or relatives.
realLife: The Labor Department's 2024 table shows 23 percent of unemployed jobseekers contacted friends or relatives, behind résumés (55 percent) and contacting employers directly (51 percent). Seekers used 1.8 methods on average.
sources: Bureau of Labor Statistics, CPS table 34 on job search methods of the unemployed, 2024: https://www.bls.gov/cps/data/aa2024/cpsaat34.htm
inGame: Job-lost call from a friend or relative is one of several job-search moves; the share is a sanity check, not a target.

turns.summary: The job seeker sends applications only and never reaches out to friends or relatives.
turns.writesBack: No lead from a tie, and the search drags on.

turns.summary: The job seeker calls every friend and relative they know within a week.
turns.writesBack: Several ties are used, a few favors are owed, and one lead may turn up.

turns.summary: A friend hears the news and calls with a lead before the person asks.
pulledBy: a layoff event the friend heard about
turns.writesBack: The friend tie gets closer and a promise to introduce is made.
